_comment: AP Cybersecurity 2.4: physical security, read the way an analyst actually reads it.
WHY A BADGE LOG AND NOT A FLOORPLAN
The player is a simulated terminal, not a widget canvas. A click-the-vulnerability
floorplan would need engine work; a log does not. It is also the truer exercise:
a physical control leaves its evidence in a log, and Unit 2 is where students
first meet detection as a skill rather than a topic.
WHY ONLY EXISTING COMMANDS
Every check here is satisfiable with ls, cd, cat, grep and wc, all of which
public/lab-player.js already implements. Nothing in this file requires a new
command. 4.2 (hashing) would have needed sha256sum, which is why this lab is
first rather than that one.
WHY graded:false
Same reason as 1.2, and it must stay in step with it. scripts/seed-manifest.js
deliberately does not seed ap-cybersecurity: that course carries its own
denominators (course_denominators and course_unit_denominators, see
docs/cyber-denominator-gaps.md). A manifest row here would add points to every
cyber student's denominator through a second path, which is the exact failure
smoke/manifest-prune.js exists to prevent.
Playable and self-checking today, records nothing. Flipping it is this one field
plus a seed run, once the cyber denominator work closes.
THE THREE FINDINGS, AND THE DECOYS
Real: B-1077 exits with no entry (tailgating), B-1055 enters at 02:47
(after hours), B-1023 appears in two buildings 8 minutes apart when the walk is
25 (cloned badge).
Decoys: B-1004 works late but badges in AND out legitimately; B-1090 has two
entries in one minute at the same door, which is a double-tap, not an attack.
The decoys are the lab. Finding three anomalies in a clean log is easy; deciding
which anomalies are attacks is the skill.
No em-dashes, per repo convention.
title: Read the badge log
page_title: AP Cybersecurity Terminal Lab: Read the Badge Log | Topic 2.4
seo_description: A week of badge swipes: three real attacks, two innocent oddities. Work the log with grep and tell them apart. Free AP Cybersecurity Topic 2.4 lab.
brief: You are covering the security desk at Northgate Labs for the week. The badge readers write every swipe to a log, and nobody has read it in months.
Three things in this week's log are attacks. Two more look wrong and are not. Your job is to tell them apart.
1. `ls` and `cd logs` to find what the desk keeps.
2. `cat doors.txt` first. You cannot judge a swipe without knowing where the doors are.
3. `cat week.csv` to see the shape of it, then stop reading it whole.
4. `grep B-1023 week.csv` pulls one badge's day out of the noise. That is the move.
5. `wc -l week.csv` counts lines when you want a denominator.
Every row is `time,badge,door,direction`. A person who is inside should have an entry. A person who is outside should have an exit. When that does not balance, somebody got in without swiping.

questions.prompt: One badge records an exit on Tuesday with no entry that day. What most likely happened?
options: The reader failed, so the entry was simply not recorded
The holder entered behind somebody else without swiping, then swiped normally on the way out
The badge was stolen and used only to leave the building
The log rotated and the entry is in last week's file
questions.explain: This is tailgating, and the exit is what exposes it. Doors that require a swipe to leave are specifically there to make the imbalance visible. A failed reader is possible, which is why you check whether that door recorded other swipes that morning: it did, so the reader was working.

questions.prompt: B-1055 enters at 02:47 on Wednesday. B-1004 enters at 21:10 on Monday and leaves at 23:40. Which is the security concern?
options: Both, because any access outside 08:00 to 18:00 is unauthorised
Neither, because both holders have valid badges
B-1055 only, because 02:47 has no matching exit and no work order, while B-1004 badges in and out cleanly during an evening
B-1004 only, because working late is more suspicious than a single early entry
questions.explain: A valid badge is not the question; the pattern is. B-1004 looks like a person working late and leaves a complete round trip. B-1055 enters in the small hours, never exits, and matches no maintenance window. Flagging every after-hours swipe is how a team learns to ignore the alert that matters.

questions.prompt: B-1023 swipes into Building A at 09:12 and into Building C at 09:20. doors.txt says the walk between them is 25 minutes. What does this indicate?
options: The badge has been cloned, because one person cannot be in both places
The building clocks are out of sync and this is a logging artefact
Building C's reader is misconfigured and logs the wrong badge
questions.explain: Impossible travel. Two physical presences from one credential means the credential exists twice. The other options are worth ruling out and the log lets you: the same two readers agree on timestamps for every other badge that morning, so the clocks are fine.
